title: Choose the visual world for E-Sahulat
question: The roll assigned Token Hall. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Token Hall
options.lineage: Passport office token halls and their bilingual green-and-white wayfinding
options.thesis: Every question is issued a token and called to the counter that can honestly serve it.
options.viewport: Green signage rail with Ask, Knowledge base, Evaluation; centre: question desk and the printed token slip with the decision; right: a Now serving board of this session's tokens.
options.risk: A queue can read as waiting; the slip must print instantly and the LED numerals stay a signature, not wallpaper.

raised.raise: Knowledge base becomes a whole-cell grid of the 30 coded passages; every citation jumps to its cell.
The passage code (F01 to F30) is the primary handle everywhere, set like a counter number.
English and Urdu sit mirrored about a centre spine in evidence, LTR left, RTL right.
Trace and evaluation numbers set in tabular figures at real data density.
Evaluation uses one strict hairline module system instead of floating cards.

options.label: Attested True Copy
options.lineage: Gazetted-officer attestation stamps on photocopied documents
options.thesis: Every answer is a photocopy of the official line, stamped and signed as a true copy.
options.viewport: Top bar and tabs; the quote sits as a copied strip with a violet verified true copy stamp over its corner and the source line beneath.
options.risk: Stamps are the familiar official move most runs reach for, and stamp texture tips into kitsch fast.

options.label: Lexicon, Shoulder and Plate
options.thesis: Each passage is a lexicon entry; colour lives only inside bordered plates.
options.viewport: Guide words in the head rule naming the passages in view; answer as a hanging entry with apparatus; decision as a bordered colour plate.
options.case: Fuses cleanly with verbatim quoting and wins on precision, but a European reference book is not a citizen's world.
options.risk: Cream and serif lands on the bookish default and distances Urdu readers.

options.label: Convention Catalog
options.thesis: Thousands of coded cells mapped to a hall.
options.viewport: Packed thumbnail grid keyed to a hall map.
options.case: Loses both axes: no citizen identification, too dense to ask from.
options.kept: Whole-cell coded grid for the 30 passages, with jump-to-cell citations.

options.label: Factory Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Everything is a numbered catalog entry.
options.viewport: A fac number and one plot on black.
options.case: Loses both axes: coded labels fight clarity for citizens.
options.kept: Catalog-number discipline: passage codes as the headline handle.

options.label: High-density Web
options.thesis: Pack every module edge to edge.
options.case: Loses both axes: overwhelms a phone user with one question.
options.kept: One strict hairline module system for the Evaluation screen.

options.label: Dance Score
options.thesis: A vertical staff with mirrored columns.
options.case: Loses both axes: notation is foreign to the task.
options.kept: Bilateral symmetry: English and Urdu mirrored about a centre spine.

options.label: Datamatics
options.case: Loses both axes: hostile to a citizen in a hurry.
options.kept: Tabular numerals at true data density for trace and metrics.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean government-services assistant: white, black type, one green accent, chat bubbles.
canonCard.viewport: Header, tabs, chat thread with source cards under each reply.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every gov chatbot by design.
